title: Octavia Spencer and Hannah Waddingham Just Made the Best Action Comedy of the Summer. It Lands on Prime Video Tomorrow.
excerpt: Ride or Die is Thelma and Louise meets Ted Lasso — an Oscar winner and a comedy queen doing their own stunts across Europe, with Bill Nighy pulling the strings. All eight episodes drop July 15.
body:
There's a moment in the *Ride or Die* trailer where **Hannah Waddingham** — six feet of impeccable tailoring and barely concealed menace — reveals to **Octavia Spencer** that she's an international assassin. Spencer's face does something extraordinary. It doesn't scream. It doesn't gasp. It just... recalibrates. That single look tells you everything about why this show works.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=QFGAxkTRAG8</youtube>

**Ride or Die** drops all eight episodes on **Amazon Prime Video** tomorrow, July 15, and it might be the most purely enjoyable thing to land on a streaming platform this summer. Created by **Tessa Coates** and directed by **Peyton Reed** — yes, the *Ant-Man* guy — the action comedy follows two best friends whose relationship gets violently complicated when one of them turns out to have a second career in contract killing.

Spencer plays **Debbie Claybourne**, the friend who does not know. Waddingham plays **Judith Burton**, the friend who very much does. When a figure from Judith's past resurfaces and a hit goes spectacularly wrong, the two women are forced to go on the run across Europe together — dodging assassins, law enforcement, and some extremely dangerous criminals, all while trying not to kill each other.

## A Cast That Has No Business Being This Good

The names around the leads are absurd. **Bill Nighy** plays a character called The Director — the kind of name that tells you everything about the tone — a shadowy figure who runs the organisation Judith works for. **Ed Skrein** is Billy Donovan, presumably someone you don't want following you. **Sylvia Hoeks**, who was terrifying as Luv in *Blade Runner 2049*, shows up as Ana. **Calam Lynch**, **Savannah Steyn**, and **Jamie Parker** round out a supporting cast that reads like a European thriller wishlist.

The showrunner is **Matt Miller**, who previously ran *Peacemaker* for DC — so expect the violence to be stylish and the comedy to be pitch-black. The Muschietti siblings, **Andy and Barbara**, who gave us *IT* and the upcoming *Welcome to Derry*, are executive producers. This show wasn't assembled. It was curated.

## They Did Their Own Stunts

The real headline is what Spencer and Waddingham put themselves through to make this. Both women — who also executive produce — performed their own stunts. Waddingham trained in combat, gunplay, and weapons handling across the entire six-month production.

> "I could never have dreamt that I would be able to learn and discipline myself to get to that stage." — Hannah Waddingham

Spencer, an Academy Award winner for *The Help* with additional nominations for *Hidden Figures* and *The Shape of Water*, described hearing the initial pitch as unlike anything in her career:

> "I've heard hundreds of pitches throughout my career and none like that one. It just had you spellbound, on the edge of your seat." — Octavia Spencer

She said she "married on the first date" — committing to the show before anyone else was attached. Waddingham's jaw dropped when she got the email saying Spencer wanted to Zoom. "To play this character opposite Octavia is getting a dream role," she said.

## Why This Matters for the Weekend Queue

The show's poster, an intentional nod to *Thelma & Louise*, tells you the emotional core beneath the explosions: this is a story about choosing a person over everything else. When Nighy's Director demands Judith pick between the organisation and Debbie, the answer isn't even close. "She's the most important thing in the world to me," Judith says. Then presumably shoots someone.

Prime Video is releasing all eight episodes simultaneously in over 240 countries. No fragmented scheduling across regions. No staggered release windows. No weekly drip. Just a full season, ready to go, wherever you are — which makes this the ideal binge for a summer weekend when you don't want to leave the air conditioning.

The chemistry between the leads is the kind that launches franchises. Two actors who've never shared a screen somehow feel like they've been doing this for years. If early buzz is to be believed, *Ride or Die* is the action comedy the summer needed — stylish, funny, occasionally brutal, and anchored by two women who are clearly having the time of their lives.

Clear the evening. This one's worth it.
